summary: This program stores a Boolean value \u2014 one of Python's two truth values \u2014 in a variable and prints it alongside a question. It is the smallest possible demonstration of the bool type.

lines.text: True is a Boolean value, not text: it is written with a capital T and no quotation marks. Writing "True" instead would store a string, and Python would treat it as a completely different kind of data.
Passing print two arguments separated by a comma lets it show a piece of text and the value of a variable together, inserting a single space between them for you.
Naming Boolean variables as yes-or-no questions, like is_sunny or has_paid, makes later code such as if is_sunny: read almost like English.
